analysis: Triamterene is a potassium-sparing diuretic that primarily works by inhibiting sodium reabsorption in the distal nephron, leading to potassium retention. Therefore, it is unlikely to cause hypokalemia (option opd) and is more likely to cause hyperkalemia. Muscle cramps (option opb) can occur as a side effect of electrolyte imbalances, but they are not a direct effect of triamterene. It does not improve glucose tolerance (option opa) nor does it typically decrease urea levels (option opc). Thus, none of the options accurately describe the primary effects of triamterene.
